title.zh: 卷三十 列傳第二十四: 蕭濟 陸瓊 顧野王 傅縡
title.en: Volume 30: Xiao Ji; Lu Qiong; Gu Yewang; Fu Zai
title.raw: 卷三十 列傳第二十四: 蕭濟 陸瓊 顧野王 傅縡 Volume 30: Xiao Ji; Lu Qiong; Gu Yewang; Fu Zai

sentences.zh: 陳書卷三十

translations.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 30
translations.idiomatic: Book of Chen, Volume 30

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十四

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Twenty-four
translations.idiomatic: Biographies, Part Twenty-four

sentences.zh: 蕭濟 陸瓊 子從典 顧野王 傅縡 章華

translations.literal: Xiao Ji; Lu Qiong; his son Congdian; Gu Ye; Fu Zhi; Zhang Hua
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ji; Lu Qiong; his son Congdian; Gu Ye; Fu Zhi; Zhang Hua

sentences.zh: 蕭濟字孝康，東海蘭陵人也。

translations.literal: Xiao Ji, styled Xiaokang, was a native of Lanling in Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ji, styled Xiaokang, came from Lanling in Donghai commandery.

sentences.zh: 少好學，博通經史，諮梁武帝左氏疑義三十餘條，尚書僕射范陽張纘、太常卿南陽劉之遴並與濟討論，纘等莫能抗對。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning and was broadly versed in the classics and histories; he submitted more than thirty items of doubt in the Zuo Commentary to Liang's Emperor Wu, and the Masters of Writing for the People Zhang Zuan of Fanyang and the Minister of Ceremonies Liu Zhiliao of Nanyang both discussed them with Ji—Zuan and the others could not stand against him.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he loved books and mastered the classics and histories. He put more than thirty questions on the Zuo Commentary before Liang's Emperor Wu; Zhang Zuan of Fanyang, vice director of the masters of writing, and Liu Zhiliao of Nanyang, minister of ceremonies, debated them with him—and could not hold their ground.

sentences.zh: 解褐梁祕書郎，遷太子舍人。

translations.literal: On leaving the purple he was made Secretariat Gentleman of Liang and promoted to groom of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a Liang secretariat gentleman, then became groom of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 預平侯景之功，封松陽縣侯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: He took part in pacifying Hou Jing and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Songyang, fief five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He shared in the campaign that crushed Hou Jing and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Songyang, with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 及高祖作鎮徐方，以濟為明威將軍、征北長史。

translations.literal: When the Founder held the frontier post at Xuzhou, he made Ji Bright Prestige General and chief secretary on the northern campaign staff.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder was holding Xuzhou as his command, he made Ji bright-prestige general and chief secretary on the northern campaign staff.

sentences.zh: 承聖二年，徵為中書侍郎，轉通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chengsheng he was summoned as Secretariat Vice Director and moved to regular attendant of the communicating scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In Chengsheng year 2 (553) he was summoned as secretariat vice director, then made regular attendant of the communicating scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 世祖為會稽太守，又以濟為宣毅府長史，遷司徒左長史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was interior administrator of Kuaiji, he again made Ji chief secretary of the Firm Resolution establishment and promoted him to left chief secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen governed Kuaiji, he again made Ji chief secretary of the firm-resolution establishment and soon promoted him to left chief secretary of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，授侍中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Ji was made palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded, Ji was made palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 尋遷太府卿，丁所生母憂，不拜。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to grand steward of the imperial household; he mourned his birth mother and did not accept the post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was named grand steward of the imperial household, but mourning his birth mother he declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 濟毗佐二主，恩遇甚篤，賞賜加於凡等。

translations.literal: Ji assisted two rulers and received favor of exceptional depth; rewards and gifts exceeded the common run.
translations.idiomatic: Ji served two sovereigns with uncommon trust; rewards and gifts outstripped the usual measure.

sentences.zh: 歷守蘭陵、陽羨、臨津、臨安等郡，所在皆著聲績。

translations.literal: In succession he held Lanling, Yangxian, Linjin, and Lin'an—wherever he went his reputation and achievement stood out.
translations.idiomatic: He governed in turn Lanling, Yangxian, Linjin, and Lin'an, and everywhere left a name for solid achievement.

sentences.zh: 太建初，入為五兵尚書，與左僕射徐陵、特進周弘正、度支尚書王瑒、[1]散騎常侍袁憲俱侍東宮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taijian he entered court as Minister of the Five Armies; together with Left Vice Director Xu Ling, Special Emeritus Zhou Hongzheng, Minister of Revenue Wang Chang, Editorial footnote marker 1. Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant Yuan Xian, he all attended the eastern palace.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Taijian (569) he entered court as minister of the five armies, and with left vice director Xu Ling, special emeritus Zhou Hongzheng, minister of revenue Wang Chang, [1] and scattered-cavalry regular attendant Yuan Xian he attended the eastern palace together.

sentences.zh: 復為司徒長史。

translations.literal: He again became chief secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He again became chief secretary of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋授度支尚書，領羽林監。

translations.literal: Soon he was given Minister of Revenue and additionally led the Feathered Forest guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made minister of revenue and also led the feathered forest guard.

sentences.zh: 遷國子祭酒，領羽林如故。

translations.literal: He was moved to libationer of the National University, still leading the Feathered Forest as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to libationer of the national university while still leading the feathered forest.

sentences.zh: 加金紫光祿大夫，兼安德宮衛尉。

translations.literal: He was given the additional posts of Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and concurrently Defender of the Secure Virtue Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon and concurrently defender of the secure virtue palace.

sentences.zh: 尋遷仁威將軍、揚州長史。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to Benevolent Prestige General and chief secretary of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made benevolent-prestige general and chief secretary of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 高宗嘗敕取揚州曹事，躬自省覽，見濟條理詳悉，文無滯害，乃顧謂左右曰「我本期蕭長史長於經傳，不言精練繁劇，乃至於此」。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan once ordered the Yangzhou bureau records taken for his own inspection; seeing Ji's entries orderly and thorough, the documents without obstruction or harm, he turned to those beside him and said, "I had expected Chief Secretary Xiao to excel in the classics—who would have said he was this skilled at intricate administration as well?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan once ordered the Yangzhou bureau papers brought for his own reading. Ji had arranged everything with meticulous clarity, the documents flowing without snag or tangle. The emperor turned to his attendants and said, "I expected Chief Secretary Xiao to shine in the classics—not that he would master tangled administration to this degree."

sentences.zh: 遷祠部尚書，加給事中，復為金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was moved to Minister of Ceremonies, given the additional post of Supervising Censor, and again made Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He was made minister of ceremonies, given the additional post of supervising censor, and again made grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 未拜而卒，時年六十六。

translations.literal: Before he could take up the appointment he died, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take office he died, at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 詔贈本官，官給喪事。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted his last office and supplied funeral expenses from the government.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted his last office posthumously and supplied his funeral from the treasury.

sentences.zh: 陸瓊字伯玉，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Lu Qiong, styled Boyu, was a native of Wu in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qiong, styled Boyu, came from Wu in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖完，梁琅邪、彭城二郡丞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wan was Liang's chief clerk in the two commanderies of Langye and Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wan was Liang's chief clerk in Langye and Pengcheng commanderies.

sentences.zh: 父雲公，梁給事黃門侍郎，掌著作。

translations.literal: His father Yungong was Liang's Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and director of composition.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yungong was Liang's attendant gentleman of the yellow gate and director of composition.

sentences.zh: 瓊幼聰惠有思理，六歲為五言詩，頗有詞采。

translations.literal: Qiong in childhood was clever and thoughtful; at six he composed pentasyllabic verse with considerable literary grace.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong as a child was quick and thoughtful. At six he wrote pentasyllabic verse with real polish.

sentences.zh: 大同末，雲公受梁武帝詔校定棋品，到溉、朱异以下並集，瓊時年八歲，於客前覆局，由是京師號曰神童。

translations.literal: At the end of Datong, Yungong received Liang's Emperor Wu's order to collate weiqi rankings; Dao Gai, Zhu Yi, and others below all gathered—Qiong was then eight sui and before the guests replayed a game from memory, whereupon the capital styled him a divine child.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Datong, Yungong received Emperor Wu of Liang's order to fix the grades of weiqi players. Dao Gai, Zhu Yi, and the rest assembled; Qiong was eight and, before the guests, reconstructed a game from memory. The capital thereafter called him a prodigy.

sentences.zh: 异言之武帝，有敕召見，瓊風神警亮，進退詳審，帝甚異之。

translations.literal: Yi spoke of him to the Emperor; an edict summoned him for audience. Qiong's bearing was alert and bright, his advance and retreat measured and careful—the Emperor marveled greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi spoke of him to the throne, and an edict called him in. Qiong's presence was keen and luminous; he moved with careful grace. The emperor was deeply struck.

sentences.zh: 十一，丁父憂，毀瘠有至性，從祖襄歎曰「此兒必荷門基，所謂一不為少」。

translations.literal: At eleven he mourned his father; his wasting grief showed utmost filial nature. His father's cousin Xiang sighed and said, "This boy will surely bear up the house—what people call 'one is not too few.'"
translations.idiomatic: At eleven he mourned his father, wasting away with a grief that showed his deepest nature. His father's cousin Xiang sighed and said, "This boy will carry the clan. As they say, one such son is not too few."

sentences.zh: 及侯景作逆，攜母避地于縣之西鄉，勤苦讀書，晝夜無怠，遂博學，善屬文。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, he took his mother to refuge in the western township of the county, toiled at reading day and night without slack, and thereby became broadly learned and skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rose in rebellion, Qiong took his mother to refuge in the county's western hamlets and read without rest by day or lamp by night, until he was broadly learned and sure with the brush.

sentences.zh: 及高宗為司徒，妙簡僚佐，吏部尚書徐陵薦瓊於高宗曰：「新安王文學陸瓊，見識優敏，文史足用，進居郎署，歲月過淹，左西掾缺，允膺茲選，階次小踰，其屈滯已積。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan was Secretariat Director he finely sifted his staff; the Minister of Personnel Xu Ling recommended Qiong to Emperor Xuan, saying: "Xin'an Prince's literary officer Lu Qiong has discerning insight, fine and quick; his literature and history suffice for use—he has served in the secretariat long, the left western aide post is vacant and he fits this selection; his rank order is slightly exceeded, but his frustration has built up.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan was secretariat director he chose his staff with care. Minister of personnel Xu Ling recommended Qiong to him, saying, "Lu Qiong, literary officer to the Prince of Xin'an, is sharp in judgment and quick in mind; his command of letters and history is ample. He has lingered in the secretariat too long. The left western aide post stands open and he should fill it—only his rank is a little low, and the delay has pressed on him too long.

sentences.zh: 」乃除司徒左西掾。

translations.literal: " He was then made left western aide of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then made left western aide of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋兼通直散騎常侍，聘齊。

translations.literal: Soon he additionally held Regular Attendant of the Communicating Scattered Cavalry and went on embassy to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also held regular attendant of the communicating scattered cavalry and went on embassy to Qi.

sentences.zh: 太建元年，重以本官掌東宮管記。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taijian he again held his former office and directed records of the eastern palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 1 (569) he again held his former post and directed the eastern palace records.

sentences.zh: 除太子庶子，兼通事舍人。

translations.literal: He was made junior mentor of the heir apparent and additionally Communicating Affairs Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was made junior mentor of the heir apparent and also communicating affairs attendant.

sentences.zh: 轉中書侍郎、太子家令。

translations.literal: He was moved to Secretariat Vice Director and steward of the heir apparent's household.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to secretariat vice director and steward of the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 長沙王為江州刺史，不循法度，高宗以王年少，授瓊長史，行江州府國事，帶尋陽太守。

translations.literal: The Prince of Changsha was inspector of Jiangzhou and did not follow law and measure; because the prince was young, Emperor Xuan gave Qiong the post of chief secretary to conduct the Jiangzhou establishment and state affairs of the commandery, and concurrently made him interior administrator of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Changsha, as inspector of Jiangzhou, ignored law and precedent. Emperor Xuan, judging him young, made Qiong his chief secretary to run the Jiangzhou establishment and the commandery's state affairs, and concurrently interior administrator of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 瓊以母老，不欲遠出，太子亦固請留之，遂不行。

translations.literal: Qiong because his mother was old did not wish to go far; the heir apparent also firmly asked to keep him—so in the end he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong's mother was old and he did not wish to travel far; the heir apparent also pressed to keep him—and so he never went.

sentences.zh: 累遷給事黃門侍郎，領羽林監。

translations.literal: In succession he was moved to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and led the Feathered Forest guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to attendant gentleman of the yellow gate and leader of the feathered forest guard.

sentences.zh: 轉太子中庶子，領步兵校尉。

translations.literal: He was moved to junior mentor in the heir apparent's household and led the Footsoldiers Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was made junior mentor in the heir apparent's household and also led the footsoldiers commandant.

sentences.zh: 又領大著作，撰國史。

translations.literal: He additionally led the Grand Composition office and compiled the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He also led the grand composition office and compiled the national history.

sentences.zh: 後主即位，直中書省，掌詔誥。

translations.literal: When Houzhu took the throne, Qiong served directly in the Secretariat and directed edicts and proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: When Houzhu succeeded, Qiong served in the secretariat itself and directed edicts and proclamations.

sentences.zh: 俄授散騎常侍，兼度支尚書，領揚州大中正。

translations.literal: Soon he was given Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant, additionally Minister of Revenue, and led the grand rectifier of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant, additionally minister of revenue, and grand rectifier of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 至德元年，除度支尚書，參掌詔誥，并判廷尉、建康二獄事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhide he was made Minister of Revenue, took part in directing edicts and proclamations, and jointly decided cases in the Court of Review and the two prisons of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide year 1 (583) he was made minister of revenue, shared in directing edicts and proclamations, and jointly judged cases in the court of review and the two Jiankang prisons.

sentences.zh: 初，瓊父雲公奉梁武帝敕撰嘉瑞記，瓊述其旨而續焉，自永定訖于至德，勒成一家之言。

translations.literal: Earlier Qiong's father Yungong had received Liang's Emperor Wu's order to compile the Record of Auspicious Omens; Qiong set forth its intent and continued it, from Yongding down to Zhide, and brought it to completion as a work in one tradition.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier his father Yungong, on Liang Emperor Wu's order, had begun the Record of Auspicious Omens. Qiong took up his aim and carried it on from Yongding through Zhide until it stood complete as a single tradition.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部尚書，著作如故。

translations.literal: He was moved to Minister of Personnel, his direction of composition unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to minister of personnel while still directing composition.

sentences.zh: 瓊詳練譜諜，雅鑒人倫，先是，吏部尚書宗元饒卒，右僕射袁憲舉瓊，高宗未之用也，至是居之，號為稱職，後主甚委任焉。

translations.literal: Qiong was thorough in genealogies and registers and refined in judging human worth. Earlier, when Minister of Personnel Zong Yuanrao died, Right Vice Director Yuan Xian had recommended Qiong, but Emperor Xuan had not yet used him; now that he held the post, he was called fully equal to the charge, and Houzhu relied on him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong knew genealogies and registers down to the last line and judged men with a quiet eye. When Minister of Personnel Zong Yuanrao died, right vice director Yuan Xian had recommended him, but Emperor Xuan had not yet appointed him. Now that he held the office, men said he filled it; Houzhu entrusted him without reserve.

sentences.zh: 瓊性謙儉，不自封植，雖位望日隆，而執志愈下。

translations.literal: Qiong's nature was modest and frugal; he did not aggrandize himself. Though rank and expectation rose day by day, his resolve grew only more humble.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong was modest and frugal and never built himself up. Though rank and renown climbed, his resolve sank lower still.

sentences.zh: 園池室宇，無所改作，車馬衣服，不尚鮮華，四時祿俸，皆散之宗族，家無餘財。

translations.literal: Garden, pond, house, and hall—he altered none of them; carriage, horse, and dress—he did not pursue fresh splendor; the seasonal salary of each season he gave away to his clan, and his house held no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He changed neither garden nor hall; his carriages and robes never chased new brilliance; each season's stipend he scattered among his kin, and no coin remained at home.

sentences.zh: 暮年深懷止足，思避權要，恆謝病不視事。

translations.literal: In his later years he deeply felt that enough was enough and wished to avoid the powerful; he constantly pleaded illness and did not attend to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he felt he had enough and sought to step back from power; again and again he pleaded illness and would not govern.

sentences.zh: 俄丁母憂，去職。

translations.literal: Soon he mourned his mother and left office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he mourned his mother and left office.

sentences.zh: 初，瓊之侍東宮也，母隨在官舍，後主賞賜優厚。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Qiong attended the eastern palace, his mother followed him in the official quarters; Houzhu rewarded them generously.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiong had served the eastern palace, his mother lived with him in the official quarters, and Houzhu had rewarded them generously.

sentences.zh: 及喪柩還鄉，詔加賻贈，并遣謁者黃長貴持冊奠祭，後主又自製誌銘，朝野榮之。

translations.literal: When the coffin returned to his home district, an edict added funeral gifts and also sent the Herald Huang Changgui with a patent to offer libation and sacrifice; Houzhu himself composed the epitaph inscription, and court and countryside alike honored him.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin went home, an edict added funeral gifts and sent herald Huang Changgui with a patent to offer libation and sacrifice. Houzhu himself wrote the epitaph, and court and countryside alike took it as honor.

sentences.zh: 瓊哀慕過毀，以至德四年卒，時年五十。

translations.literal: Qiong's grief for his mother exceeded measure; in the fourth year of Zhide he died, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong's grief for his mother passed all bounds. In Zhide year 4 (586) he died, at fifty.

sentences.zh: 詔贈領軍將軍，官給喪事。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made him General of the Palace Guard and supplied funeral expenses from the government.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him general of the palace guard and supplied his funeral from the treasury.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷行於世。

translations.literal: A collection in twenty juan circulated in his day.
translations.idiomatic: A collection in twenty juan circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 長子從宜，仕至武昌王文學。

translations.literal: His eldest son Congyi reached the post of literary officer to the Prince of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Congyi rose to literary officer to the Prince of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 第三子從典，字由儀。

translations.literal: His third son Congdian, styled Youyi.
translations.idiomatic: His third son Congdian, styled Youyi.

sentences.zh: 幼而聰敏。

translations.literal: From childhood he was clever and keen.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was clever and keen.

sentences.zh: 八歲，讀沈約集，見回文研銘，從典援筆擬之，便有佳致。

translations.literal: At eight he read Shen Yue's collected works; seeing a palindrome study inscription, Congdian took up the brush and imitated it, and at once achieved fine effect.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he read Shen Yue's collected works. Seeing a palindrome study inscription, Congdian took up the brush to match it and at once produced something fine.

sentences.zh: 年十三，作柳賦，其詞甚美。

translations.literal: At thirteen he composed a Rhapsody on the Willow; its wording was very beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he wrote a Rhapsody on the Willow, and its language was very fine.

sentences.zh: 瓊時為東宮管記，宮僚並一時俊偉，瓊示以此賦，咸奇其異才。

translations.literal: At that time Qiong was director of the eastern palace records; the palace staff were all outstanding men of the age—Qiong showed them this rhapsody, and all marveled at his unusual talent.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong was then directing the eastern palace records; the palace staff were all men of mark in their day. He showed them the rhapsody, and each wondered at the boy's gift.

sentences.zh: 從父瑜特所賞愛，及瑜將終，家中墳籍皆付從典，從典乃集瑜文為十卷，仍製集序，其文甚工。

translations.literal: His father's cousin Yu especially cherished and loved him; when Yu was near death he entrusted the household's grave registers and books all to Congdian. Congdian thereupon collected Yu's writings into ten juan and also composed a preface to the collection—the writing was very accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: His father's cousin Yu cherished him above the rest. When Yu was dying he entrusted the household's grave registers and books to Congdian, who gathered Yu's writings into ten juan and wrote a preface—the prose was accomplished throughout.

sentences.zh: 從典篤好學業，博涉群書，於班史尤所屬意。

translations.literal: Congdian deeply loved learning and was broadly versed in many books; in the History of the Former Han he took special interest.
translations.idiomatic: Congdian loved learning deeply and ranged through many books; the History of the Former Han was his particular passion.

sentences.zh: 年十五，本州舉秀才。

translations.literal: At fifteen his home province nominated him as a cultivated talent.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen his home province nominated him as cultivated talent.

sentences.zh: 解褐著作佐郎，轉太子舍人。

translations.literal: On leaving the purple he was made composition aide and moved to groom of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as composition aide, then became groom of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 時後主賜僕射江總并其父瓊詩，總命從典為謝啟，俄頃便就，文華理暢，總甚異焉。

translations.literal: At that time Houzhu bestowed verse on Vice Director Jiang Zong and his father Qiong together; Zong ordered Congdian to compose the letter of thanks—in a moment it was done, the writing elegant and the reasoning clear, and Zong marveled greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu then bestowed verse on vice director Jiang Zong and on his father Qiong together. Zong had Congdian draft the letter of thanks; in a moment it stood finished, elegant in word and clear in reason, and Zong was astonished.

sentences.zh: 尋授信義王文學，轉太子洗馬。

translations.literal: Soon he was made literary officer to the Prince of Xinyi and moved to groom who washes the heir apparent's horses.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made literary officer to the Prince of Xinyi, then groom who washes the heir apparent's horses.

sentences.zh: 又遷司徒左西掾，兼東宮學士。

translations.literal: He was again moved to left western aide of the Secretariat and additionally academician of the eastern palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made left western aide of the secretariat and additionally academician of the eastern palace.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂去職。

translations.literal: He mourned his father and left office.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned his father and left office.

sentences.zh: 尋起為德教學士，固辭不就，後主敕留一員，以待從典。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as academician of the Virtue Teaching establishment; he firmly declined and did not accept—Houzhu ordered one post kept vacant, awaiting Congdian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned as academician of the virtue-teaching establishment; he firmly declined. Houzhu ordered one post kept vacant, waiting for Congdian.

sentences.zh: 俄屬金陵淪沒，隨例遷關右。

translations.literal: Soon Jinling fell; following precedent he was moved to the region west of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jinling fell; by precedent he was moved west of the passes.

sentences.zh: 仕隋為給事郎，兼東宮學士。

translations.literal: Under Sui he served as Attendant Gentleman and additionally academician of the eastern palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui he served as attendant gentleman and additionally academician of the eastern palace.

sentences.zh: 又除著作佐郎。

translations.literal: He was again made composition aide.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made composition aide.

sentences.zh: 右僕射楊素奏從典續司馬遷史記迄于隋，其書未就。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Yang Su memorialized that Congdian should continue Sima Qian's Records of the Historian down to Sui—the book was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: Right vice director Yang Su memorialized that Congdian should continue Sima Qian's Records of the Historian down to Sui; the book was never finished.

sentences.zh: 值隋末喪亂，寓居南陽郡，以疾卒，時年五十七。

translations.literal: When the turmoil at the end of Sui came, he lodged in Nanyang commandery and died of illness, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the chaos at the end of Sui he lodged in Nanyang commandery and died of illness, at fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 顧野王字希馮，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Gu Ye, styled Xifeng, was a native of Wu in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Ye, styled Xifeng, came from Wu in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖子喬，梁東中郎武陵王府參軍事。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ziqiao was a staff officer in the Eastern Central Army Prince of Wuling's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ziqiao was a staff officer in the eastern central army establishment of the Prince of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 父烜，信威臨賀王記室，兼本郡五官掾，以儒術知名。

translations.literal: His father Xuan was recorder for the Trustworthy Prestige Prince of Linhe and concurrently the five offices chief clerk of his home commandery; he was known for Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xuan was recorder for the trustworthy-prestige Prince of Linhe and concurrently five-offices chief clerk of his home commandery, known for Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 野王幼好學。

translations.literal: Ye from childhood loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: Ye loved learning from childhood.

sentences.zh: 七歲，讀五經，略知大旨。

translations.literal: At seven he read the Five Classics and grasped their main purport.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he read the Five Classics and grasped their main purport.

sentences.zh: 九歲能屬文，嘗製日賦，領軍朱异見而奇之。

translations.literal: At nine he could compose prose; he once wrote a Rhapsody on the Sun, and the Area Commander Zhu Yi, on seeing it, marveled.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he could write prose. He once composed a Rhapsody on the Sun; area commander Zhu Yi read it and marveled.

sentences.zh: 年十二，隨父之建安，撰建安地記二篇。

translations.literal: At twelve he followed his father to Jian'an and composed two chapters of a Topography of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he followed his father to Jian'an and wrote two chapters of a Topography of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 長而遍觀經史，精記嘿識，天文地理、蓍龜占候、蟲篆奇字，無所不通。

translations.literal: When grown he surveyed the classics and histories in full, with keen memory and silent retention; astronomy and geography, milfoil and tortoise divination, insect scripts and strange characters—there was nothing he did not penetrate.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he ranged through the classics and histories with a memory that held without effort; astronomy and geography, milfoil and tortoise divination, insect scripts and strange characters—nothing lay outside his reach.

sentences.zh: 梁大同四年，除太學博士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Datong of Liang he was made Erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang Datong year 4 (538) he was made erudite of the national university.

sentences.zh: 遷中領軍臨賀王府記室參軍。

translations.literal: He was moved to recorder in the staff of the Central Army Prince of Linhe's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to recorder in the staff of the central army Prince of Linhe's establishment.

sentences.zh: 宣

translations.literal: Xuan
translations.idiomatic: Xuan

translations.literal: Collation variant: (Cheng).
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (Cheng).

sentences.zh: 〔 城〕王為揚州刺史，[2]野王及琅邪王褒並為賓客，王甚愛其才。

translations.literal: Collation variant: [city] served as inspector of Yangzhou, Editorial footnote marker 2. Gu Ye and Wang Bao of Langye were both retainers; the prince greatly cherished their talent.
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: [city], the prince served as inspector of Yangzhou, [2] and Gu Ye and Wang Bao of Langye were both his retainers; the prince greatly prized their gifts.

sentences.zh: 野王又好丹青，善圖寫，王於東府起齋，乃令野王畫古賢，命王褒書贊，時人稱為二絕。

translations.literal: Ye also loved cinnabar green and was skilled at drawing and depiction; the prince raised a studio in the eastern mansion and had Ye paint the ancient worthies and Wang Bao compose encomia—men of the time called them the twin marvels.
translations.idiomatic: Ye also loved ink and color and was skilled at drawing. The prince built a studio in the eastern mansion, had Ye paint the ancient worthies and Wang Bao write their praises—men of the time called the pair a double wonder.

sentences.zh: 及侯景之亂，野王丁父憂，歸本郡，乃召募鄉黨數百人，隨義軍援京邑。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing's turmoil came, Ye was mourning his father and returned to his home commandery; he then recruited several hundred men of his native place and followed the loyal army to relieve the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing's rebellion broke out, Ye was mourning his father and went home; he then recruited several hundred men of his township and marched with the loyal army to relieve the capital.

sentences.zh: 野王體素清羸，裁長六尺，又居喪過毀，殆不勝衣，及杖戈被甲，陳君臣之義，逆順之理，抗辭作色，見者莫不壯之。

translations.literal: Ye's frame had always been slight and frail; he was barely six chi tall, and in mourning he had wasted beyond bearing clothes—yet when he took spear and donned armor, set forth the righteousness of ruler and minister and the principle of obedience and rebellion, and spoke with defiant color, all who saw him felt emboldened.
translations.idiomatic: Ye had always been slight of build, barely six feet, and in mourning had wasted until his robes hung loose—yet when he took spear and donned armor, spoke of the bond between ruler and minister and the line between loyalty and rebellion, and flushed with defiance as he spoke, every witness felt his spirit rise.

sentences.zh: 京城陷，野王逃會稽，尋往東陽，與劉歸義合軍據城拒賊。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, Ye fled to Kuaiji, then went on to Dongyang, and with Liu Guiyi united armies to hold the city and resist the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, Ye fled to Kuaiji, then went to Dongyang and joined Liu Guiyi in holding the city against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 侯景平，太尉王僧辯深嘉之，使監海鹽縣。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified, Grand Marshal Wang Sengbian praised him deeply and had him oversee Haiyan county.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing was crushed, grand marshal Wang Sengbian praised him deeply and made him overseer of Haiyan county.

sentences.zh: 野王少以篤學至性知名，在物無過辭失色，觀其容貌，似不能言，及其勵精力行，皆人所莫及。

translations.literal: Ye from youth was known for devoted learning and utmost nature; among others he never overstepped in word or lost color in countenance—to look at his face, he seemed unable to speak—yet when he exerted his strength and acted, none could match him.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Ye was known for devoted learning and deep feeling. Among others he never overspoke or let his face slip—to see him, you would think he could not speak at all—yet when he set his will and moved, no one could keep pace.

sentences.zh: 第三弟充國早卒，野王撫養孤幼，恩義甚厚。

translations.literal: His third younger brother Chongguo died early; Ye raised the orphaned young with deep kindness and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His third younger brother Chongguo died young; Ye raised the orphaned children with deep kindness.

sentences.zh: 其所撰著玉篇三十卷，輿地志三十卷，符瑞圖十卷，顧氏譜傳十卷，分野樞要一卷，續洞冥紀一卷，玄象表一卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: What he compiled and wrote—the Jade Chapters in thirty juan, Topographies of the Realm in thirty juan, Diagrams of Auspicious Omens in ten juan, Genealogical Traditions of the Gu Clan in ten juan, Essentials of the Division of the Heavens in one juan, Continuation of the Records of the Hidden Realm in one juan, Tables of the Dark Signs in one juan—all circulated in his day.
translations.idiomatic: What he wrote and compiled—the Jade Chapters in thirty juan, Topographies of the Realm in thirty juan, Diagrams of Auspicious Omens in ten juan, Genealogical Traditions of the Gu Clan in ten juan, Essentials of the Division of the Heavens in one juan, Continuation of the Records of the Hidden Realm in one juan, Tables of the Dark Signs in one juan—all circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 又撰通史要略一百卷，國史紀傳二百卷，未就而卒。

translations.literal: He also drafted Essentials of the Comprehensive History in one hundred juan and National History in Annals and Biographies in two hundred juan, but died before completion.
translations.idiomatic: He also drafted Essentials of the Comprehensive History in one hundred juan and National History in Annals and Biographies in two hundred juan, but died before either was finished.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 傅縡字宜事，北地靈州人也。

translations.literal: Fu Zai, styled Yishi, was a man of Lingzhou in Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zai, styled Yishi, was from Lingzhou in Beidi.

sentences.zh: 父彝，梁臨沂令。

translations.literal: His father Yi was Liang's magistrate of Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi was Liang's magistrate of Linyi.

sentences.zh: 縡幼聰敏，七歲誦古詩賦至十餘萬言。

translations.literal: Zai was clever as a child; at seven he could recite ancient poems and rhapsodies to more than a hundred thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: Zai was clever as a child; at seven he could recite ancient poems and rhapsodies totaling more than a hundred thousand words.

sentences.zh: 長好學，能屬文。

translations.literal: When grown he loved learning and could compose literature.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he loved learning and could compose literature.

sentences.zh: 梁太清末，攜母南奔避難，俄丁母憂，在兵亂之中，居喪盡禮，哀毀骨立，士友以此稱之。

translations.literal: At the end of Liang's Taiqing era he fled south with his mother to escape disaster; soon he suffered his mother's mourning; amid martial chaos he observed mourning rites fully, wasting away to skin and bone, and scholars praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Liang's Taiqing era he fled south with his mother; soon his mother died. Amid the chaos of war he observed mourning rites fully and wasted to skin and bone, and scholars praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 後依湘州刺史蕭循，循頗好士，廣集墳籍，縡肆志尋閱，因博通群書。

translations.literal: Later he relied on Xiao Xun, inspector of Xiangzhou; Xun greatly favored scholars and broadly gathered canonical writings; Zai indulged his will in seeking and reading and thus mastered all books.
translations.idiomatic: Later he relied on Xiao Xun, inspector of Xiangzhou. Xun favored scholars and gathered many books; Zai read at will and came to master all fields of learning.

sentences.zh: 王琳聞其名，引為府記室。

translations.literal: Wang Lin heard his fame and brought him in as recorder of the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin heard his fame and made him recorder of the staff.

sentences.zh: 琳敗，隨琳將孫瑒還都。

translations.literal: When Lin was defeated, he followed Lin's general Sun Chang back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin was defeated, he followed Lin's general Sun Chang back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時世祖使顏晃賜瑒雜物，瑒託縡啟謝，詞理優洽，文無加點，晃還言之世祖，尋召為撰史學士。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Wu sent Yan Huang to present Sun Chang with various goods; Chang entrusted Zai to draft the letter of thanks; the reasoning was excellent and fluent and the text needed no correction; when Huang returned he reported this to Emperor Wu, and soon Zai was summoned as compiler-historian.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Wu sent Yan Huang to present Sun Chang with gifts. Chang had Zai draft the letter of thanks; the reasoning was excellent and the text needed no correction. Huang reported this to Emperor Wu, and Zai was soon summoned as compiler-historian.

sentences.zh: 除司空府記室參軍，遷驃騎安成王中記室，撰史如故。

translations.literal: He was appointed recorder of the staff in the bureau of the Minister of Works, then transferred to central recorder for Prince Ancheng of the Pacer Cavalry, compiling history as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made recorder in the bureau of the minister of works, then central recorder for Prince Ancheng of the pacer cavalry, still compiling history.

sentences.zh: 縡篤信佛教，從興皇惠朗法師受三論，[3]盡通其學。

translations.literal: Zai devoutly believed in Buddhism; from Master Huilang of Xinghuang he received the Three Treatises, [3] and fully penetrated that learning.
translations.idiomatic: Zai was a devout Buddhist. He received the Three Treatises from Master Huilang of Xinghuang [3] and fully mastered the school.

sentences.zh: 時有大心暠法師著無諍論以詆之，縡乃為明道論，用釋其難。

translations.literal: At that time the monk Daxin Hao wrote the Treatise on Non-Contention to attack him; Zai thereupon wrote the Treatise on Illuminating the Way to explain the difficulties.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the monk Daxin Hao wrote the Treatise on Non-Contention to attack him; Zai answered with the Treatise on Illuminating the Way to resolve the objections.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：

translations.literal: Its summary says:
translations.idiomatic: Its summary says:

sentences.zh: 無諍論言：比有弘三論者，雷同訶詆，恣言罪狀，歷毀諸師，非斥眾學，論中道而執偏心，語忘懷而競獨勝，方學數論，更為讎敵，讎敵既搆，諍鬥大生，以此之心，而成罪業，罪業不止，豈不重增生死，大苦聚集？

translations.literal: The Treatise on Non-Contention says: Recently there are those who promote the Three Treatises, echoing one another in reviling and slander, freely speaking charges, successively destroying all masters, rejecting and expelling the many schools, talking of the middle way yet holding a biased mind, speaking of forgetting cares yet competing to be uniquely victorious; just learning several treatises they become each other's foes; once foes are joined, great disputing arises; with such a mind they form karmic offenses; offenses unceasing—will they not again add to birth and death and the great gathering of suffering?
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on Non-Contention says: Lately those who promote the Three Treatises echo one another in reviling and slander, freely speak charges, destroy master after master, and reject the many schools. They talk of the middle way yet hold a biased mind; they speak of forgetting cares yet compete to win alone. Learning several treatises, they become each other's foes; once foes are joined, great disputing arises. With such a mind they form karmic offenses; offenses unceasing—will they not heap up birth, death, and great suffering?

sentences.zh: 答曰：三論之興，為日久矣。

translations.literal: The reply says: The rise of the Three Treatises has been long.
translations.idiomatic: The reply says: The rise of the Three Treatises has been long.

sentences.zh: 龍樹創其源，除內學之偏見；

translations.literal: Nagarjuna founded its source, removing the biased views of inner learning;
translations.idiomatic: Nagarjuna founded its source, removing the biased views of inner learning;

sentences.zh: 提婆揚其旨，蕩外道之邪執。

translations.literal: Deva spread its aim, sweeping away the heterodox clinging of outer paths.
translations.idiomatic: Deva spread its aim, sweeping away the heterodox clinging of outer paths.

sentences.zh: 欲使大化流而不擁，玄風闡而無墜。

translations.literal: They wished to make the great teaching flow without obstruction and the mysterious wind be opened without falling.
translations.idiomatic: They wished the great teaching to flow without obstruction and the mysterious wind to spread without falling.

sentences.zh: 其言曠，其意遠，其道博，其流深。

translations.literal: Its words are vast, its meaning far, its way broad, its current deep.
translations.idiomatic: Its words are vast, its meaning far, its way broad, its current deep.

sentences.zh: 斯固龍象之騰驤，鯤鵬之摶運。

translations.literal: This is truly the soaring of dragon and elephant, the whirl of kun and peng.
translations.idiomatic: This is truly the soaring of dragon and elephant, the whirl of kun and peng.

translations.literal: (jian)
translations.idiomatic: [jian]—emended below.

sentences.zh: 〔蹇〕乘決羽，[4]豈能觖望其閒哉？

translations.literal: [lame] riding sky-plumes, [4] how can one strain to peer into that interval?
translations.idiomatic: [Lame] riding sky-plumes, [4] how can one strain to peer into that interval?

sentences.zh: 頃代澆薄，時無曠士，苟習小學，以化蒙心，漸染成俗，遂迷正路，唯競穿鑿，各肆營造，枝葉徒繁，本源日翳，一師解釋，復異一師，更改舊宗，各立新意，同學之中，取寤復別，如是展轉，添糅倍多。

translations.literal: In recent generations customs are shallow and thin; the age lacks broad-minded scholars; they merely learn petty doctrines to transform dull minds; gradual dyeing becomes custom and they lose the right road; they only compete in forced interpretations, each freely fabricating; branches and leaves grow vainly while the root source is daily obscured; one master's explanation again differs from another's; they change the old school and each sets up a new intent; among fellow students they wake and part again; thus turning and turning, admixture multiplies ever more.
translations.idiomatic: Recent generations are shallow; the age lacks broad-minded scholars. Men learn petty doctrines to dull their minds; custom takes hold and they lose the right road. They compete in forced interpretations and each fabricates freely; branches multiply while the root is obscured. One master's explanation differs from another's; they change the old school and each sets up a new intent; fellow students wake and part again—turning thus, admixture multiplies.

sentences.zh: 總而用之，心無的准；

translations.literal: Taking it all together to use, the mind has no mark to aim at;
translations.idiomatic: Taken all together, the mind has no mark to aim at;

sentences.zh: 擇而行之，何者為正？

translations.literal: choosing what to practice, which is correct?
translations.idiomatic: choosing what to practice, which is correct?

sentences.zh: 豈不渾沌傷竅，嘉樹弊牙？

translations.literal: Is this not wounding the undifferentiated by piercing it and harming the fine tree by breaking its shoots?
translations.idiomatic: Is this not wounding the undifferentiated by piercing it and harming the fine tree by breaking its shoots?

sentences.zh: 雖復人說非馬，家握靈蛇，以無當之卮，同畫地之餅矣。

translations.literal: Though again men speak of the non-horse and households grasp the spirit serpent, it is like a measureless cup or a cake drawn on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Though men speak of the non-horse and households grasp the spirit serpent, it is like a measureless cup or a cake drawn on the ground.

sentences.zh: 其於失道，不亦宜乎？

translations.literal: For losing the Way, is it not fitting?
translations.idiomatic: For losing the Way, is it not fitting?

sentences.zh: 攝山之學，則不如是。

translations.literal: The learning of She Mountain is not like this.
translations.idiomatic: The learning of She Mountain is not like this.

sentences.zh: 守一遵本，無改作之過；

translations.literal: It keeps to one and follows the root, without the fault of altering and making anew;
translations.idiomatic: It keeps to one and follows the root, without altering and making anew;

sentences.zh: 約文申意，杜臆斷之情。

translations.literal: it contracts the text to express the meaning and blocks the mood of arbitrary judgment.
translations.idiomatic: it contracts the text to express the meaning and blocks arbitrary judgment.

sentences.zh: 言無預說，理非宿構。

translations.literal: Words are not pre-spoken; principle is not long composed.
translations.idiomatic: Words are not pre-spoken; principle is not long composed.

sentences.zh: 睹緣爾乃應，見敵然後動。

translations.literal: Seeing conditions, then one responds; seeing an opponent, then one moves.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing conditions, one responds; seeing an opponent, one moves.

sentences.zh: 縱橫絡驛，忽怳杳冥。

translations.literal: Vertically and horizontally they weave like post relays, suddenly dim and remote.
translations.idiomatic: Vertically and horizontally they weave like post relays, suddenly dim and remote.

sentences.zh: 或彌綸而不窮，或消散而無所。

translations.literal: Sometimes they extend the net without end, sometimes they dissolve and have no place.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes they extend the net without end, sometimes they dissolve and have no place.

sentences.zh: 煥乎有文章，蹤朕不可得；

translations.literal: Brilliant, there is pattern; tracks and traces cannot be obtained;
translations.idiomatic: Brilliant in pattern; tracks and traces cannot be obtained;

sentences.zh: 深乎不可量，即事而非遠。

translations.literal: deep, it cannot be measured—present in the affair yet not far.
translations.idiomatic: deep beyond measure—present in the affair yet not far.

sentences.zh: 凡相酬對，隨理詳覈。

translations.literal: Whenever they answer one another, they follow principle and examine in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they answer one another, they follow principle and examine in detail.

sentences.zh: 有何嫉詐，干犯諸師？

translations.literal: What jealousy and deceit is there in offending the various masters?
translations.idiomatic: What jealousy or deceit is there in offending the various masters?

sentences.zh: 且諸師所說，為是可毀？

translations.literal: Moreover, what the various masters said—can it be destroyed?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, can what the various masters said be destroyed?

sentences.zh: 為不可毀？

translations.literal: Or can it not be destroyed?
translations.idiomatic: Or can it not be destroyed?

sentences.zh: 若可毀者，毀故為衰；

translations.literal: If it can be destroyed, destruction therefore is decline;
translations.idiomatic: If it can be destroyed, destruction is decline;

sentences.zh: 若不可毀，毀自不及。

translations.literal: if it cannot be destroyed, destruction itself does not reach it.
translations.idiomatic: if it cannot be destroyed, destruction does not reach it.

sentences.zh: 法師何獨蔽護不聽毀乎？

translations.literal: Why does the Master alone shield and protect and not allow destruction?
translations.idiomatic: Why does the master alone shield and forbid destruction?

sentences.zh: 且教有大小，備在聖誥，大乘之文，則指斥小道。

translations.literal: Moreover teaching has great and small, fully set forth in the sage's instructions; the texts of the Great Vehicle then point and reproach the small path.
translations.idiomatic: Teaching has great and small, fully set forth in the sage's instructions; the Great Vehicle texts reproach the small path.

sentences.zh: 今弘大法，寧得不言大乘之意耶？

translations.literal: Now in promoting the great teaching, can one fail to speak the intent of the Great Vehicle?
translations.idiomatic: Now in promoting the great teaching, can one fail to speak the intent of the Great Vehicle?

sentences.zh: 斯則褒貶之事，從弘放學；

translations.literal: Then praise and blame follow from broad promotion of learning;
translations.idiomatic: Then praise and blame follow from broad promotion of learning;

sentences.zh: 與奪之辭，依經議論。

translations.literal: words of granting and taking away rely on the sutras for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: words of granting and taking away rely on the sutras for discussion.

sentences.zh: 何得見佛說而信順，在我語而忤逆？

translations.literal: How can one see the Buddha's words and believe and follow, yet in my words be contrary and rebellious?
translations.idiomatic: How can one believe and follow the Buddha's words yet be contrary and rebellious to mine?

sentences.zh: 無諍平等心如是耶？

translations.literal: Is this the equal mind of non-contention?
translations.idiomatic: Is this the equal mind of non-contention?

sentences.zh: 且忿恚煩惱，凡夫恆性，失理之徒，率皆有此。

translations.literal: Moreover anger and affliction are the constant nature of ordinary men; those who lose principle mostly all have this.
translations.idiomatic: Anger and affliction are the constant nature of ordinary men; those who lose principle mostly have this.

sentences.zh: 豈可以三脩未愜，六師懷恨，而蘊涅槃妙法，永不宣揚？

translations.literal: How can one, because the three cultivations are not satisfied and the six masters harbor resentment, store the wonderful dharma of nirvana and never proclaim it?
translations.idiomatic: How can one, because the three cultivations are not satisfied and the six masters harbor resentment, store the wonderful dharma of nirvana and never proclaim it?

sentences.zh: 但冀其忿憤之心既極，恬淡之寤自成耳。

translations.literal: One only hopes that when the mind of anger and resentment has reached its limit, the awakening of calm detachment will form of itself.
translations.idiomatic: One only hopes that when anger and resentment reach their limit, calm detachment will form of itself.

sentences.zh: 人面不同，其心亦異，或有辭意相反，或有心口相符。

translations.literal: Human faces differ and their hearts also differ; some have words and intent opposed, some have heart and mouth agreeing.
translations.idiomatic: Faces differ and hearts differ; some speak one way and mean another, some heart and mouth agree.

sentences.zh: 豈得必謂他人說中道而心偏執，己行無諍，外不違而內平等？

translations.literal: How can one insist that when others speak the middle way their minds are biased and clinging, while one's own practice is non-contention, outwardly not violating yet inwardly equal?
translations.idiomatic: How can one insist that when others speak the middle way their minds are biased, while one's own practice is non-contention—outwardly compliant yet inwardly equal?

sentences.zh: 讎敵鬥訟，豈我事焉；

translations.literal: Foes' quarrels and lawsuits—how is that my affair?
translations.idiomatic: Foes' quarrels and lawsuits—how is that my affair?

sentences.zh: 罪業聚集，鬥諍者所畏耳。

translations.literal: The gathering of karmic offenses is what disputants fear.
translations.idiomatic: The gathering of karmic offenses is what disputants fear.

sentences.zh: 無諍論言：攝山大師誘進化導，則不如此，即習行於無諍者也。

translations.literal: The Treatise on Non-Contention says: The great master of She Mountain in enticing, advancing, transforming, and guiding is not like this—he is one who practiced and walked in non-contention.
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on Non-Contention says: The great master of She Mountain in enticing, advancing, transforming, and guiding was not like this—he practiced non-contention.

sentences.zh: 導悟之德既往，淳一之風已澆，競勝之心，呵毀之曲，盛於茲矣。

translations.literal: The virtue of guiding and awakening is past; the wind of pure unity is already diluted; the mind competing for victory and the tune of reviling and destroying flourish in this age.
translations.idiomatic: The virtue of guiding and awakening is past; the wind of pure unity is diluted; the mind of competing for victory and the tune of reviling flourish now.

sentences.zh: 吾願息諍以通道，讓勝以忘德。

translations.literal: I wish to rest contention to open the Way and yield victory to forget virtue.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to rest contention to open the Way and yield victory to forget virtue.

sentences.zh: 何必排拂異家，生其恚怒者乎？

translations.literal: Why must one exclude and brush away other schools and breed their anger?
translations.idiomatic: Why must one exclude other schools and breed their anger?

sentences.zh: 若以中道之心行於成實，亦能不諍；

translations.literal: If with the mind of the middle way one practices the Chengshi, one also can be without contention;
translations.idiomatic: If with the mind of the middle way one practices the Chengshi, one also can be without contention;

sentences.zh: 若以偏著之心說於中論，亦得有諍。

translations.literal: if with a biased, clinging mind one speaks the Middle Treatises, one also may have contention.
translations.idiomatic: if with a biased, clinging mind one speaks the Middle Treatises, one also may have contention.

sentences.zh: 固知諍與不諍，偏在一法。

translations.literal: One therefore knows that contention and non-contention depend on a single dharma.
translations.idiomatic: One therefore knows that contention and non-contention depend on a single dharma.

sentences.zh: 答曰：攝山大師實無諍矣，但法師所賞，未衷其節。

translations.literal: The reply says: The great master of She Mountain was truly without contention, but what the Master prizes does not hit his measure.
translations.idiomatic: The reply says: The great master of She Mountain was truly without contention, but what the master prizes does not hit his measure.

sentences.zh: 彼靜守幽谷，寂爾無為，凡有訓勉，莫匪同志，從容語嘿，物無閒然，故其意雖深，其言甚約。

translations.literal: He quietly kept to a secluded valley, silent and without acting; whenever there was instruction, none were not of one mind; in ease of speech or silence nothing was out of place—therefore though his meaning was deep, his words were very few.
translations.idiomatic: He quietly kept to a secluded valley, silent and without acting; all who were instructed were of one mind; in speech or silence nothing was out of place—though his meaning was deep, his words were few.

sentences.zh: 今之敷暢，地勢不然。

translations.literal: Today's spreading and exposition—the terrain is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Today's spreading and exposition—the terrain is not so.

sentences.zh: 處王城之隅，居聚落之內，呼吸顧望之客，脣吻縱橫之士，奮鋒穎，勵羽翼，明目張膽，被堅執銳，騁異家，衒別解，窺伺閒隙，邀冀長短，與相酬對，捔其輕重，豈得默默無言，唯唯應命？

translations.literal: Dwelling in a corner of the royal city, living within a settlement, guests who breathe and look about, men whose lips and tongues run crosswise—they sharpen points and edges, stir wings, open eyes wide and bare their courage, don armor and grasp sharp weapons, gallop other schools, display separate explanations, peep and watch for gaps, invite and hope for strengths and weaknesses, answer one another and wrestle their weight—how can one silently say nothing and only yes-yes obey orders?
translations.idiomatic: Dwelling in a corner of the royal city, living within a settlement, guests who breathe and look about, men whose lips run crosswise—they sharpen points, stir wings, open eyes and bare courage, don armor and grasp weapons, gallop other schools, display separate explanations, watch for gaps, invite comparison, answer and wrestle for weight—how can one stay silent and only yes-yes obey?

sentences.zh: 必須掎摭同異，發擿玼瑕，忘身而弘道，忤俗而通教，以此為病，益知未達。

translations.literal: One must pick out sameness and difference, expose flaws, forget the body to spread the Way and go against custom to penetrate teaching; to take this as illness shows one knows one has not attained.
translations.idiomatic: One must pick out sameness and difference, expose flaws, forget the body to spread the Way and go against custom to penetrate teaching; to take this as illness shows one has not attained.

sentences.zh: 若令大師當此之地，亦何必默己，而為法師所貴耶？

translations.literal: If the great master were in this place, why must he silence himself yet be prized by the Master?
translations.idiomatic: If the great master were in this place, why must he silence himself yet be prized by the master?

sentences.zh: 法師又言：「吾願息諍以通道，讓勝以忘德。

translations.literal: The Master also said: "I wish to rest contention to open the Way and yield victory to forget virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The master also said, "I wish to rest contention to open the Way and yield victory to forget virtue.

sentences.zh: 」道德之事，不止在諍與不諍，讓與不讓也。

translations.literal: " Matters of virtue and the Way are not only in contending or not contending, yielding or not yielding.
translations.idiomatic: " Matters of virtue and the Way are not only in contending or not contending, yielding or not yielding.

sentences.zh: 此語直是人閒所重，法師慕而言之，竟未知勝若為可讓也。

translations.literal: This saying is simply what the human world esteems; the Master admires it and speaks it, yet in the end does not know how victory can be yielded.
translations.idiomatic: This saying is simply what the world esteems; the master admires it and speaks it, yet does not know how victory can be yielded.

sentences.zh: 若他人道高，則自勝不勞讓矣；

translations.literal: If another's Way is high, then victory of itself needs no yielding;
translations.idiomatic: If another's Way is high, victory needs no yielding;

sentences.zh: 他人道劣，則雖讓而無益矣。

translations.literal: if another's Way is low, then though one yields it is of no benefit.
translations.idiomatic: if another's Way is low, yielding brings no benefit.

sentences.zh: 欲讓之辭，將非虛設？

translations.literal: Words of wishing to yield—are they not empty setup?
translations.idiomatic: Words of wishing to yield—are they not empty setup?

sentences.zh: 中道之心，無處不可。

translations.literal: The mind of the middle way has no place where it cannot be.
translations.idiomatic: The mind of the middle way has no place where it cannot be.

sentences.zh: 成實三論，何事致乖？

translations.literal: Chengshi and Three Treatises—what matter makes them diverge?
translations.idiomatic: Chengshi and Three Treatises—what makes them diverge?

sentences.zh: 但須息守株之解，除膠柱之意，是事皆中也。

translations.literal: One need only rest the interpretation of guarding a stump and remove the intent of gluing the peg; in these matters all are centered.
translations.idiomatic: One need only rest the interpretation of guarding a stump and remove the intent of gluing the peg; in these matters all are centered.

sentences.zh: 來旨言「諍與不諍，偏在一法」。

translations.literal: Your message says "contention and non-contention depend on a single dharma."
translations.idiomatic: Your message says "contention and non-contention depend on a single dharma."

sentences.zh: 何為獨褒無諍耶？

translations.literal: Why alone praise non-contention?
translations.idiomatic: Why alone praise non-contention?

sentences.zh: 詎非矛楯？

translations.literal: Is this not spear and shield?
translations.idiomatic: Is this not spear and shield?

sentences.zh: 無諍論言：邪正得失，勝負是非，必生於心矣，非謂所說之法，而有定相論勝劣也。

translations.literal: The Treatise on Non-Contention says: Wrong and right, gain and loss, victory and defeat, and is and is-not must arise in the mind; it is not that the dharma spoken has a fixed mark by which to discuss superiority and inferiority.
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on Non-Contention says: Wrong and right, gain and loss, victory and defeat must arise in the mind; the dharma spoken has no fixed mark for judging superiority.

sentences.zh: 若異論是非，以偏著為失言，無是無非，消彼得失，以此論為勝妙者，他論所不及，此亦為失也。

translations.literal: If in different treatises on is and is-not one takes biased clinging as faulty speech, and no-is and no-is-not dissolve gain and loss, and with this treatise as supremely victorious beyond what other treatises reach—this also is fault.
translations.idiomatic: If one takes biased clinging as faulty, dissolves gain and loss in no-is and no-is-not, and holds this treatise supreme beyond others—that also is fault.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: How so?

sentences.zh: 凡心所破，豈無心於能破，則勝負之心不忘，寧不存勝者乎？

translations.literal: Whatever the mind destroys, is there not a mind in the one who can destroy? Then the mind of victory and defeat is not forgotten—will it not still harbor the victor?
translations.idiomatic: Whatever the mind destroys, is there not a mind in the destroyer? Then the mind of victory and defeat is not forgotten—does it not still harbor the victor?

sentences.zh: 斯則矜我為得，棄他之失，即有取捨，大生是非，便是增諍。

translations.literal: Then one prides oneself as having got it and abandons another's fault; thereupon is taking and rejecting, greatly producing is and is-not—this is increasing contention.
translations.idiomatic: Then one prides oneself as right and abandons another's fault; taking and rejecting arise and is and is-not grow—this increases contention.

sentences.zh: 答曰：言為心使，心受言詮；

translations.literal: The reply says: Words are the mind's envoy; the mind receives words' explication;
translations.idiomatic: The reply says: Words are the mind's envoy; the mind receives words' explication;

sentences.zh: 和合根塵，鼓動風氣，故成語也。

translations.literal: joining roots and dust, stirring wind and qi, therefore words are formed.
translations.idiomatic: joining roots and dust, stirring wind and qi, therefore words are formed.

sentences.zh: 事必由心，實如來說。

translations.literal: Affairs must come from the mind, as the Tathagata said.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs must come from the mind, as the Tathagata said.

sentences.zh: 至於心造偽以使口，口行詐以應心，外和而內險，言隨而意逆，求利養，引聲名，入道之人，在家之士，斯輩非一。

translations.literal: As for the mind making falsity to employ the mouth and the mouth practicing deceit to answer the mind, outwardly harmonious yet inwardly dangerous, words following yet intent opposing, seeking profit and support and drawing fame—those who enter the Way and gentlemen at home, such are not one.
translations.idiomatic: The mind may make falsity to employ the mouth and the mouth practice deceit to answer the mind—outwardly harmonious yet inwardly dangerous, words following yet intent opposing, seeking profit and fame. Those who enter the Way and gentlemen at home—such are not few.

sentences.zh: 聖人所以曲陳教誡，深致防杜，說見在之殃咎，敘將來之患害，此文明著，甚於日月，猶有忘愛軀，冒峻制，蹈湯炭，甘虀粉，必行而不顧也。

translations.literal: The sage therefore bent his teaching and deeply set up guards and blocks, speaking present calamities and guilt and narrating coming miseries and harms; this pattern is bright and clear, more than sun and moon—yet there are those who forget love of body, brave stern prohibition, tread boiling coals and sweeten chaff powder, certain to act and not look back.
translations.idiomatic: The sage therefore bent his teaching and set up guards, speaking present calamities and future harms; this is brighter than sun and moon—yet some forget love of body, brave stern prohibition, tread boiling coals and sweeten chaff powder, and act without looking back.

sentences.zh: 豈能悅無諍之作，而回首革音耶？

translations.literal: How can they be pleased by compositions on non-contention and turn their heads to change their tune?
translations.idiomatic: How can they be pleased by compositions on non-contention and turn to change their tune?

sentences.zh: 若弘道之人，宣化之士，心知勝也，口言勝也，心知劣也，口言劣也，亦無所苞藏，亦無所忌憚，但直心而行之耳。

translations.literal: If men who spread the Way and gentlemen who proclaim transformation know in mind they are victorious and in mouth speak victory, know in mind they are inferior and in mouth speak inferiority, they also have nothing hidden and nothing feared—they only act with a straight mind.
translations.idiomatic: If those who spread the Way know in mind they are victorious and speak victory, know they are inferior and speak inferiority, they hide nothing and fear nothing—they only act with a straight mind.

sentences.zh: 他道雖劣，聖人之教也；

translations.literal: Another's Way though inferior is still the sage's teaching;
translations.idiomatic: Another's Way though inferior is still the sage's teaching;

sentences.zh: 己德雖優，亦聖人之教也。

translations.literal: one's own virtue though superior is also the sage's teaching.
translations.idiomatic: one's own virtue though superior is also the sage's teaching.

sentences.zh: 我勝則聖人勝，他劣則聖人劣。

translations.literal: If I am victorious then the sage is victorious; if another is inferior then the sage is inferior.
translations.idiomatic: If I am victorious the sage is victorious; if another is inferior the sage is inferior.

sentences.zh: 聖人之優劣，蓋根緣所宜爾。

translations.literal: The sage's superiority and inferiority are probably what roots and conditions make fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The sage's superiority and inferiority are probably what roots and conditions make fitting.

sentences.zh: 於彼於此，何所厚薄哉？

translations.literal: Regarding that and this, what partiality or thickness is there?
translations.idiomatic: Regarding that and this, what partiality is there?

sentences.zh: 雖復終日按劍，極夜擊柝，瞋目以爭得失，作氣以求勝負，在誰處乎？

translations.literal: Though one may all day hand on sword, all night beat the watch, glare to struggle over gain and loss, and work up breath to seek victory and defeat—in whom does it rest?
translations.idiomatic: Though one may clutch a sword all day and beat the night watch, glare to fight over gain and loss, and work up breath to win or lose—in whom does it finally rest?

sentences.zh: 有心之與無心，徒欲分別虛空耳。

translations.literal: Minded and unminded—they merely wish to distinguish empty space.
translations.idiomatic: Minded versus unminded—they only try to carve distinctions in empty space.

sentences.zh: 何意不許我論說，而使我謙退？

translations.literal: Why the intent not to allow me to discourse but to make me yield and withdraw?
translations.idiomatic: Why refuse to let me argue and instead make me yield and withdraw?

sentences.zh: 此謂鷦

translations.literal: This is to say—the jiao
translations.idiomatic: This is to say—the jiao

translations.literal: (peng)
translations.idiomatic: (peng)

sentences.zh: 〔敕〕已翔於寥廓，[5]而虞者猶窺藪澤而求之。

translations.literal: [imperial edict] has already soared into the vast sky, [5] yet the lookout still peeks into marshes seeking it.
translations.idiomatic: [The imperial edict] has already soared into the vast sky, [5] yet the apprehensive still peek into marshes seeking it.

sentences.zh: 嗟乎！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 丈夫當弘斯道矣。

translations.literal: A true man ought to spread this Way.
translations.idiomatic: A true man ought to spread this Way.

sentences.zh: 無諍論言：無諍之道，通於內外。

translations.literal: The Non-Contention Treatise says: the way of non-contention penetrates within and without.
translations.idiomatic: The Non-Contention Treatise says: the way of non-contention runs through inner and outer alike.

sentences.zh: 子所言須諍者，此用末而救本，失本而營末者也。

translations.literal: What you say must be contended—this uses the branch to save the root and loses the root while tending the branch.
translations.idiomatic: When you say one must contend, that uses the branch to save the root and loses the root while tending the branch.

sentences.zh: 今為子言之。

translations.literal: Now I will speak to you on it.
translations.idiomatic: Now I will explain it to you.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: How so?

sentences.zh: 若依外典，尋書契之前，至淳之世，朴質其心，行不言之教，當于此時，民至老死不相往來，而各得其所，復有何諍乎？

translations.literal: If one follows external classics and seeks before written contracts, in the utmost pure age hearts were plain and simple and the teaching of wordlessness was practiced—at that time the people to old age did not visit one another, yet each obtained his place; what contention was there again?
translations.idiomatic: If one follows secular classics back before written records, in the most pristine age hearts were plain and the wordless teaching held sway—then people lived to old age without visiting one another, yet each had his place; what contention could there be?

sentences.zh: 固知本

translations.literal: Thus one knows the root
translations.idiomatic: Thus one knows the root

translations.literal: (lai)
translations.idiomatic: (lai)

sentences.zh: 〔末〕不諍，[6]是物之真矣。

translations.literal: [end] does not contend, [6] which is the truth of things.
translations.idiomatic: [The end] does not contend, [6] which is the truth of things.

sentences.zh: 答曰：諍與無諍，不可偏執。

translations.literal: He replied: contention and non-contention cannot be one-sidedly clung to.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: contention and non-contention cannot be clung to one-sidedly.

sentences.zh: 本之與末，又安可知？

translations.literal: Root and branch—how again can one know?
translations.idiomatic: Root and branch—how can one know for certain?

sentences.zh: 由來不諍，寧知非末？

translations.literal: From of old not contending—how does one know it is not the branch?
translations.idiomatic: If from of old there is no contention, how do you know that is not the branch?

sentences.zh: 於今而諍，何驗非本？

translations.literal: Contending today—what proof that it is not the root?
translations.idiomatic: If one contends today, what proof that it is not the root?

sentences.zh: 夫居後而望前，則為前；

translations.literal: Standing behind and looking forward, then it is forward;
translations.idiomatic: Standing behind and looking forward, that is forward;

sentences.zh: 居前而望後，則為後。

translations.literal: standing in front and looking back, then it is back.
translations.idiomatic: standing in front and looking back, that is behind.

sentences.zh: 而前後之事猶如彼此，彼呼此為彼，此呼彼為彼，彼此之名，的居誰處？

translations.literal: Yet matters of before and after are still like this and that—that calls this "that," this calls that "that"; the name of this and that—who truly occupies the place?
translations.idiomatic: Yet before and after are like this and that—each side calls the other "that"; the names this and that—who really holds the place?

sentences.zh: 以此言之，萬事可知矣。

translations.literal: Spoken thus, the myriad affairs can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Put this way, the myriad affairs become knowable.

sentences.zh: 本末前後，是非善惡，可恆守邪？

translations.literal: Root and branch, before and after, right and wrong, good and evil—can they be eternally held?
translations.idiomatic: Root and branch, before and after, right and wrong, good and evil—can any of them be held forever?

sentences.zh: 何得自信聰明，廢他耳目？

translations.literal: How can one trust one's own cleverness and discard others' ears and eyes?
translations.idiomatic: How can one trust one's own cleverness and discard others' ears and eyes?

sentences.zh: 夫水泡生滅，火輪旋轉，入牢阱，受羈紲，生憂畏，起煩惱，其失何哉？

translations.literal: Water bubbles arise and perish, the fire-wheel turns—entering the pit trap, receiving fetters, giving birth to worry and fear, raising vexations—what is the loss?
translations.idiomatic: Water bubbles rise and burst, the fire-wheel spins—one enters the pit, wears fetters, breeds worry and fear, and raises vexations—what is lost?

sentences.zh: 不與道相應，而起諸見故也。

translations.literal: Not corresponding to the Way and therefore raising the various views—that is why.
translations.idiomatic: It is because one fails to correspond to the Way and instead raises fixed views.

sentences.zh: 相應者則不然，無為也，無不為也。

translations.literal: Those who correspond are not so—there is non-action, and there is nothing not done.
translations.idiomatic: Those who correspond are otherwise—there is non-action, and there is nothing left undone.

sentences.zh: 善惡不能偕，而未曾離善惡，生死不能至，亦終然在生死，故得永離而任放焉。

translations.literal: Good and evil cannot go together, yet one has never left good and evil; birth and death cannot arrive, yet one is ultimately still in birth and death—therefore one can forever leave and let go.
translations.idiomatic: Good and evil cannot coincide, yet one never leaves them; birth and death cannot be reached, yet one remains in them—therefore one can forever leave and let go.

sentences.zh: 是以聖人念繞桎之不脫，愍黏膠之難離，故殷勤教示，備諸便巧。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage, mindful that winding bonds are not shed and pitying how sticky glue is hard to leave, earnestly teaches and shows, providing every expedient.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the sage, seeing that winding bonds are not shed and pitying how sticky glue is hard to leave, earnestly teaches and provides every expedient.

sentences.zh: 希向之徒，涉求有類，雖驎角難成，象形易失，寧得不髣彿遐路，勉勵短晨？

translations.literal: Those who hope for the goal, crossing and seeking, have their kinds; though unicorn horns are hard to complete and images are easy to lose, how can one not take the distant road as model and urge on the short morning?
translations.idiomatic: Seekers on the path still have their kind; though a unicorn's horn is hard to finish and likenesses slip away, how can one not take the far road as model and press on through the brief dawn?

sentences.zh: 且當念己身之善惡，莫揣他物，而欲分別，而言我聰明，我知見，我計校，我思惟，以此而言，亦為疏矣。

translations.literal: One should only reflect on good and evil in one's own person, not measure other things and wish to distinguish, saying "I am clever, my insight, my reckoning, my thinking"—spoken thus, it is also crude.
translations.idiomatic: One should reflect on the good and evil in oneself, not measure other things and try to divide them up, saying "I am clever, I see, I reckon, I think"—that too is crude.

sentences.zh: 他人者實難測，或可是凡夫真爾，亦可是聖人俯同，時俗所宜見，果報所應睹。

translations.literal: Other people are truly hard to measure; they may indeed be ordinary men as they seem, or they may be sages bending to match what custom at the time should see and what karmic retribution should display.
translations.idiomatic: Others are truly hard to fathom; they may be ordinary men as they seem, or sages stooping to what the times should see and what karmic retribution should show.

sentences.zh: 安得肆胸衿，盡情性，而生譏誚乎？

translations.literal: How can one give free rein to the breast, exhaust nature and disposition, and then breed ridicule?
translations.idiomatic: How can one give free rein to the breast, exhaust one's nature, and then breed ridicule?

sentences.zh: 正應虛己而遊乎世，俛仰於電露之閒耳。

translations.literal: One should only empty oneself and wander in the world, bowing and looking up in the space between lightning and dew.
translations.idiomatic: One should empty oneself and wander the world, bowing and rising in the span between lightning and dew.

sentences.zh: 明月在天，眾水咸見，清風至林，群籟畢響。

translations.literal: The bright moon is in the sky—all waters alike see it; the clear wind reaches the grove—all pipes together sound.
translations.idiomatic: The bright moon is in the sky and every water reflects it; the clear wind reaches the grove and every pipe sounds.

sentences.zh: 吾豈逆物哉？

translations.literal: How would I go against things?
translations.idiomatic: How would I go against things?

sentences.zh: 不入鮑魚，不甘腐鼠。

translations.literal: Not entering among salted fish, not sweet on rotten rats.
translations.idiomatic: Not entering among salted fish, not sweet on rotten rats.

sentences.zh: 吾豈同物哉？

translations.literal: How would I be the same as things?
translations.idiomatic: How would I be the same as things?

sentences.zh: 誰能知我，共行斯路。

translations.literal: Who can know me and walk this road together?
translations.idiomatic: Who can know me and walk this road with me?

sentences.zh: 浩浩乎！

translations.literal: Vast!
translations.idiomatic: Vast!

sentences.zh: 堂堂乎！

translations.literal: Majestic!
translations.idiomatic: Majestic!

sentences.zh: 豈復見有諍為非，無諍為是？

translations.literal: How again can one see contention as wrong and non-contention as right?
translations.idiomatic: How again can one treat contention as wrong and non-contention as right?

sentences.zh: 此則諍者自諍，無諍者自無諍，吾俱取而用之。

translations.literal: Then those who contend contend of themselves, and those who do not contend do not contend of themselves—I take both and use them.
translations.idiomatic: Let those who contend contend on their own and those who do not contend refrain on their own—I take both and use them.

sentences.zh: 寧勞法師費功夫，點筆紙，但申於無諍；

translations.literal: Better that the Dharma master not waste effort, dotting brush and paper, but only declare non-contention;
translations.idiomatic: Better that the Dharma master spare the effort of dotting brush and paper and only preach non-contention;

sentences.zh: 弟子疲脣舌，消晷漏，唯對於明道？

translations.literal: the disciple wear out lips and tongue, consume the sundial's drip—only facing the illumined Way?
translations.idiomatic: while the disciple wear out lips and tongue and consume the sundial's drip—only to face the illumined Way?

sentences.zh: 戲論哉！

translations.literal: Idle disputation!
translations.idiomatic: Idle disputation!

sentences.zh: 糟粕哉！

translations.literal: Dregs and lees!
translations.idiomatic: Dregs and lees!

sentences.zh: 必欲且考真偽，蹔觀得失，無過依賢聖之言，檢行藏之理，始終研究，表裏綜覈，使浮辭無所用，詐道自然消。

translations.literal: If one must for the moment examine truth and falsehood and briefly observe gain and loss, nothing surpasses relying on the words of sages and worthies, checking conduct and hiding, studying beginning and end, collating inner and outer, so that floating phrases have no use and deceitful ways naturally vanish.
translations.idiomatic: If one must for the moment test truth and falsehood and briefly weigh gain and loss, nothing surpasses relying on sages and worthies, checking conduct and intent, studying beginning and end, collating inner and outer, so floating phrases fail and deceitful ways vanish of themselves.

sentences.zh: 請待後筵，以觀其妙矣。

translations.literal: Please wait for the later session and observe its subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: Please wait for the later session and observe its subtlety.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官兼通直散騎侍郎使齊，還除散騎侍郎、鎮南始興王諮議參軍，兼東宮管記。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter, in his original office he was concurrently made unranked gentleman attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry on mission to Qi; on return he was made gentleman attendant of the scattered cavalry and adviser to the Prince of Shixing, General Who Pacifies the South, concurrently eastern palace recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, retaining his original post, he was also made unranked gentleman attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry on mission to Qi; on his return he was made gentleman attendant of the scattered cavalry and adviser to the Prince of Shixing, general who pacifies the south, while retaining his eastern palace recorder post.

sentences.zh: 歷太子庶子、僕，兼管記如故。

translations.literal: He passed through crown prince household supervisor and steward, still concurrently recorder as before.
translations.idiomatic: He served as crown prince household supervisor and steward, still keeping the recorder post.

sentences.zh: 後主即位，遷祕書監、右衛將軍，兼中書通事舍人，掌詔誥。

translations.literal: When Houzhu took the throne he was moved to director of the secretariat and right guard general, concurrently secretariat attendant for current affairs, in charge of edicts and letters.
translations.idiomatic: When Houzhu took the throne he was made director of the secretariat and right guard general, concurrently secretariat attendant for current affairs, in charge of edicts.

sentences.zh: 縡為文典麗，性又敏速，雖軍國大事，下筆輒成，未嘗起草，沉思者亦無以加焉，甚為後主所重。
