translations.literal: Zai's writing was classical and ornate; his nature was also quick and sharp—even on great affairs of army and state, when he put brush to paper it was at once complete; he never drafted beforehand, and even those who pondered deeply could not surpass him; Houzhu valued him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Zai wrote in a classical, ornate style and was quick by nature—even on great military and state affairs his brush finished at once; he never drafted beforehand, and even deep thinkers could not surpass him; Houzhu valued him greatly.

sentences.zh: 然性木彊，不持檢操，負才使氣，陵侮人物，朝士多銜之。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was wooden and strong; he did not hold to restraint and conduct, relied on talent and gave rein to temper, and insulted people—court gentlemen mostly harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was stiff by nature, held to no restraint, relied on talent and vented his temper, and insulted others—most court gentlemen resented him.

sentences.zh: 會施文慶、沈客卿以便佞親幸，專制衡軸，而縡益疏。

translations.literal: It happened that Shi Wenqing and Shen Keqing through fawning and favoritism were close and cherished, monopolizing the balance of power, while Zai grew still more distant.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Wenqing and Shen Keqing won favor through flattery, monopolized power, and Zai grew still more distant.

sentences.zh: 文慶等因共譖縡受高驪使金，後主收縡下獄。

translations.literal: Wenqing and the others therefore together slandered Zai for receiving gold from a Goguryeo envoy; Houzhu arrested Zai and put him in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Wenqing and the others then slandered Zai for taking gold from a Goguryeo envoy; Houzhu had him arrested and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 縡素剛，因憤恚，乃於獄中上書曰：「夫君人者，恭事上帝，子愛下民，省嗜慾，遠諂佞，未明求衣，日旰忘食，是以澤被區宇，慶流子孫。

translations.literal: Zai by nature was firm; in indignant rage he thereupon submitted a memorial from prison, saying: "The ruler ought to respectfully serve the Supreme Lord, love and cherish the people below, reduce cravings and desires, keep far from flattery and favoritism, at unclear dawn seek clothing, at sundown forget food—thereby grace covers the realm and blessing flows to sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Zai was by nature unyielding; in rage he submitted a memorial from prison: "A ruler should respectfully serve Heaven, love the people, curb desire, keep far from flatterers, rise at unclear dawn and forget food at sundown—then grace covers the realm and blessing reaches his heirs.

sentences.zh: 陛下頃來酒色過度，不虔郊廟之神，專媚淫昏之鬼；

translations.literal: Your Majesty of late has passed bounds in wine and sex, is not reverent toward the spirits of the suburban altars, and dotes on the ghosts of lewd darkness alone;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty of late has gone to excess in wine and sex, neglects the spirits of the suburban altars, and dotes only on ghosts of lewd darkness;

sentences.zh: 小人在側，宦豎弄權，惡忠直若仇讎，視生民如草芥；

translations.literal: petty men are at your side, palace eunuchs toy with power, you hate the loyal and straight as enemies, and regard living people as grass and stubble;
translations.idiomatic: petty men stand at your side, eunuchs toy with power, you hate the loyal and upright as enemies, and treat the people like grass;

sentences.zh: 後宮曳綺繡，廄馬餘菽粟，百姓流離，殭尸蔽野；

translations.literal: in the rear palace trailing brocade and embroidery, in the stables horses leave grain and millet surplus, while the people wander displaced and stiff corpses cover the wilds;
translations.idiomatic: the rear palace trails brocade while stable horses leave grain unused, the people wander homeless, and stiff corpses cover the wilds;

sentences.zh: 貨賄公行，帑藏損耗，神怒民怨，眾叛親離。

translations.literal: bribes go openly, the treasury is drained, the spirits are angry and the people resentful, the masses rebel and kin turn away.
translations.idiomatic: bribes run openly, the treasury drains, spirits rage and the people resent, the masses rebel and kin turn away.

sentences.zh: 恐東南王氣，自斯而盡。

translations.literal: I fear the kingly qi of the southeast ends from this.
translations.idiomatic: I fear the kingly qi of the southeast ends here.

sentences.zh: 」書奏，後主大怒。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted Houzhu was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial arrived Houzhu was furious.

sentences.zh: 頃之，意稍解，遣使謂縡曰：「我欲赦卿，卿能改過不？

translations.literal: Before long his mind eased somewhat; he sent an envoy to tell Zai: "I wish to pardon you—can you reform your faults?
translations.idiomatic: Before long his anger cooled somewhat; he sent an envoy to tell Zai, "I wish to pardon you—can you reform your faults?

sentences.zh: 」縡對曰：「臣心如面，臣面可改，則臣心可改。

translations.literal: " Zai replied: "My mind is like my face; if my face can change, then my mind can change.
translations.idiomatic: " Zai replied, "My mind is like my face; if my face can change, then my mind can change.

sentences.zh: 」後主於是益怒，令宦者李善慶窮治其事，[7]遂賜死獄中，時年五十五。

translations.literal: " Houzhu thereupon grew still more angry and ordered the eunuch Li Shanqing to investigate the matter to the end, [7] and Zai was granted death in prison, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: " Houzhu then grew still angrier and ordered the eunuch Li Shanqing to investigate to the end, [7] and Zai was ordered to die in prison, aged fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷行於世。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in ten scrolls circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: A collected works in ten scrolls circulated after his death.

sentences.zh: 時有吳興章華，字仲宗，家世農夫，至華獨好學，與士君子遊處，頗覽經史，善屬文。

translations.literal: At the time there was Zhang Hua of Wuxing, styled Zhongzong; his family for generations were farmers—to Hua alone he loved learning, associated with gentlemen and scholars, and broadly read the classics and histories, skilled at composition.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhang Hua of Wuxing, styled Zhongzong, came from a farming family—he alone loved learning, kept company with scholars, read widely in the classics and histories, and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，乃遊嶺南，居羅浮山寺，專精習業。

translations.literal: In the turmoil of Hou Jing he then traveled to Lingnan, lived at Luofu Mountain Temple, and devoted himself to study.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's turmoil he fled to Lingnan, lived at Luofu Mountain Temple, and devoted himself to study.

sentences.zh: 歐陽頠為廣州刺史，署為南海太守。

translations.literal: Ouyang Fu was inspector of Guangzhou and appointed him Administrator of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Fu, inspector of Guangzhou, appointed him administrator of Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 及歐陽紇敗，乃還京師。

translations.literal: When Ouyang He was defeated he then returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Ouyang He was defeated he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 太建中，高宗使吏部侍郎蕭引喻廣州刺史馬靖，令入子為質，引奏華與俱行。

translations.literal: In the Taichu era Emperor Gaozong sent Vice Minister of Personnel Xiao Yin to instruct Guangzhou Inspector Ma Jing to send his son in as hostage; Yin memorialized that Hua should go with him on the mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taichu era Emperor Gaozong sent Vice Minister of Personnel Xiao Yin to instruct Guangzhou inspector Ma Jing to send his son as hostage; Yin memorialized that Hua should accompany the mission.

sentences.zh: 使還，而高宗崩。

translations.literal: When the mission returned, Emperor Gaozong had died.
translations.idiomatic: When the mission returned, Emperor Gaozong had died.

sentences.zh: 後主即位，朝臣以華素無伐閱，競排詆之，乃除大市令，既雅非所好，乃辭以疾，鬱鬱不得志。

translations.literal: When Houzhu took the throne the court gentlemen, because Hua by nature had no meritorious background, all competed to slander him; he was therefore made director of the great market. As it was utterly not to his liking, he pleaded illness and resigned, depressed and without achieving his aim.
translations.idiomatic: When Houzhu took the throne, court gentlemen—Hua had no record of merit—competed to slander him; he was made director of the great market. That post ill suited him; he pleaded illness and resigned, depressed and thwarted.

sentences.zh: 禎明初，上書極諫，其大略曰：「昔高祖南平百越，北誅逆虜；

translations.literal: Early in Zhenming he submitted a memorial of extreme remonstrance; its general purport said: "In the past the Founder southward pacified the Hundred Yue and northward punished the rebellious captive;
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenming he submitted a memorial of fierce remonstrance, saying in gist: "In the past the Founder southward pacified the Hundred Yue and northward punished the rebel lord;

sentences.zh: 世祖東定吳會，西破王琳；

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu eastward settled Wu and Kuaiji and westward broke Wang Lin;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu eastward settled Wu and Kuaiji and westward broke Wang Lin;

sentences.zh: 高宗克復淮南，辟地千里：三祖之功，亦至勤矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong recovered Huainan and opened land for a thousand li—the merit of the three ancestors was also utmost diligence.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong recovered Huainan and opened land for a thousand li—the merit of the three ancestors was utmost diligence.

sentences.zh: 陛下即位，于今五年，不思先帝之艱難，不知天命之可畏，溺於嬖寵，惑於酒色，祠七廟而不出，拜妃嬪而臨軒，老臣宿將，棄之草莽，諂佞讒邪，昇之朝廷。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has reigned now five years, not thinking of the former emperor's hardships, not knowing that Heaven's mandate is to be feared, drowning in favorites, deluded by wine and sex, sacrificing at the seven temples yet not going out, bowing to consorts yet holding court, old ministers and veteran generals cast to the wild grass, flatterers and slanderous villains raised into the court.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has reigned five years without remembering the former emperor's hardships or fearing Heaven's mandate, drowning in favorites and delusion of wine and sex, sacrificing at the seven temples yet not going out, bowing to consorts yet holding court, casting old ministers and veteran generals to the wilds and raising flatterers and slanderers.

sentences.zh: 今疆埸日蹙，隋軍壓境，陛下如不改絃易張，臣見麋鹿復遊於姑蘇臺矣。

translations.literal: Now the frontier daily narrows and Sui troops press the border—if Your Majesty does not change the string and ease the bow, I see deer again roaming the Gusu Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Now the frontier shrinks daily and Sui troops press the border—if Your Majesty does not change course, I see deer roaming the Gusu Terrace again.

sentences.zh: 」書奏，後主大怒，即日命斬之。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted Houzhu was greatly enraged and that same day ordered him beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial arrived Houzhu was furious and ordered him beheaded that same day.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：蕭濟、陸瓊，俱以才學顯著，顧野王博極群典，傅縡聰警特達，並一代之英靈矣。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Xiao Ji and Lu Qiong both for talent and learning were illustrious; Gu Yewang's learning exhausted the canon; Fu Zai was sharp-witted and outstanding—all spirits of an age.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Xiao Ji and Lu Qiong both shone for talent and learning; Gu Yewang mastered the canon; Fu Zai was brilliantly sharp—all spirits of an age.

sentences.zh: 然縡不能循道進退，遂寘極網，悲夫！

translations.literal: Yet Zai could not follow the Way in advancing and withdrawing and therefore fell into the utmost net—pitiable!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zai could not advance and withdraw by the Way and so fell into the utmost net—pitiable!
